title: AetherPlay — First Experiment, Step by Step
voice: Microsoft Zira Desktop, pitch +38%, rate -9% (soft young feminine tone)

segments.text: This is AetherPlay's first experiment, step by step, on the real build — recorded live on an Android emulator. Follow along on your own phone.
Step one. Install the pair. AetherPlay Space and AetherPlay Lab must come from the same signer — grab both APKs from the release page and install them together.
Step two. Open Space, go to Session, and tap Start session. A foreground service begins, a notification appears with an Open Game button, and the bridge wakes up for Lab.

Step three. Open Crystal Sprint and catch some crystals by dragging the orb. The number on your screen is real game memory — that's what we'll search for. In this build, the game pauses honestly whenever it goes to the background, so your values stay put while you work.

Step four. Open Lab — it connects and shows the live session. Choose your value type, pick a search mode, and search. Tip: if you don't know the value, use an unknown-value search and let refinement find it — every row now shows its real live value.

Step five. Tap the result you care about. Type a new value, press Preview — you'll see old and new side by side, and read-only addresses say so — then Commit. Every write is journaled, and Undo restores it while the value is still yours.
Step six. Press Freeze in the detail sheet. The value is gently re-applied while the session lives — watch the game try to change it and fail. When you stop the session, every freeze stops. Always.

One honest note: everything you just saw works against the included cooperative training game. Popular third-party games are not supported in this build — that needs the experimental guest runtime, and this project will never fake a demo of something that doesn't exist, or touch online and competitive games.

That's the whole loop: session, play, search, preview, commit, undo, freeze, stop. Build it yourself from the repository, and read the tutorials for every recovery path. See you in the next experiment!
